objectives: Say how to make water safe.
reviewNotes: Health and hygiene advice is conservative and general; to be reviewed by a health worker or nurse. It never replaces seeing a nurse or a doctor. Water treatment advice to be checked by a health worker.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Sources
blocks.md: Water comes from **rain**, **rivers**, **springs**, **wells**, **boreholes** and **taps**. Some water is clean, and some is not safe to drink.

blocks.caption: Sources of water.
blocks.alt: Six boxes with rain, river, spring, well, borehole, tap.

blocks.title: Safe water
blocks.md: Water that is safe to drink is clear, has no bad smell, and has been treated. An adult can **boil** water for a few minutes, or use a **filter** or treatment tablets. Keep it in a clean, covered container.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Clear water can still carry germs.
- Do not drink water from a dirty pond.
- Boiled water must be kept covered.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: Rivers and wells also give water.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: How can an adult make water safer?

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Name the dry and rainy seasons.
reviewNotes: Seasons: the dry/rainy pattern differs a lot across Cameroon; keep wording general and check against the textbook.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Weather
blocks.md: Weather can be **sunny**, **cloudy**, **rainy**, **windy** or **stormy**. We can measure rain in a **rain gauge** and heat with a **thermometer**.

blocks.caption: Weather words.
blocks.alt: Five boxes: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy.

blocks.title: Seasons in Cameroon
blocks.md: In much of Cameroon there is a **dry season** (little rain) and a **rainy season** (a lot of rain). The time of the seasons is different in the north, the centre and the coast. Farmers plant at the start of the rains.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not shelter under a tree in a thunderstorm.
- Do not walk in flood water.
- The seasons differ in different regions.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: In which season do farmers plant seeds?
steps: At the start of the rainy season.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Which tool measures how hot it is?

blocks.title: Properties
blocks.md: A **property** tells what a material is like. It can be **hard** or **soft**, **rough** or **smooth**, **stretchy** or **stiff**, **waterproof** or not. We choose a material for a job by its properties.

blocks.caption: Properties.
blocks.alt: Four boxes with properties and example materials.

blocks.title: Float or sink
blocks.md: Some materials **float** on water: wood, a plastic bottle, a cork. Some **sink**: a stone, a coin, a key. Rubber is stretchy and waterproof: so boots are made of rubber.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A big thing can float and a small thing can sink (a small coin sinks, a big log floats).
- Do not test with sharp or dangerous things.
- Ask an adult to help.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Which will float: a stone or a piece of wood?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why are boots made of rubber?

Say that the Moon goes round the Earth.
reviewNotes: Simple astronomy; check wording ('goes round the Earth' / 'Earth turns') with the textbook.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: The Sun
blocks.md: The **Sun** is a star. It gives us **light** and **heat**. We see it in the day. It looks big because it is much nearer to us than the other stars.

blocks.caption: The Sun, the Earth and the Moon (not to scale).
blocks.alt: A big yellow Sun, a smaller blue Earth and a small grey Moon.

blocks.title: Moon and stars
blocks.md: The **Moon** goes round the **Earth**. It shines because it reflects light from the Sun. Its shape seems to change during the month. At night we see **stars**. They are very far away.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Never look straight at the Sun.
- The Moon does not make its own light.
- The Sun does not go round the Earth. The Earth turns, so we have day and night.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What gives us light and heat in the day?

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: It has no light of its own.
It reflects light from the Sun.

lessons.title: Safety and looking after our surroundings
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 2) — Elementary Science; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Say how to stay safe at home and school.
Reduce, reuse and put waste in the right place.
reviewNotes: Safety advice is general; check local guidance. Recycling facilities may not exist in all places.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Safety
blocks.md: Keep away from fire, hot water, electricity, sharp tools and chemicals. Never touch a dead wire. Keep medicines and chemicals away from small children. Tell a trusted adult if something is dangerous.

blocks.caption: Looking after our surroundings.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: reduce, reuse, recycle where possible.

blocks.title: Waste
blocks.md: We make waste every day. **Reduce** waste: use only what you need. **Reuse**: use a bottle again. Put rubbish in a bin. Food waste can go to a compost heap. Do not burn plastic or throw it in rivers.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not play near the road, fire or deep water.
- Do not burn plastic: the smoke is harmful.
- Wash your hands after touching rubbish.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What can you do with an empty plastic bottle?
steps: Or put it in a bin if it is broken.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: You see a fallen electric wire. What do you do?
steps: Keep away and tell an adult.
blocks.answer: Keep away and tell an adult
